title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic, paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measures the marginal effect of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the preregistered contract (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered corpus; single shared generator candidate per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; the repair step was never invoked. Primary paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. All execution, scoring, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic replay (see Disclosure). We interpret this as a ceiling/null result specific to the registered experimental contract and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation is attractive for network operations but raises safety concerns: an incorrect change can break reachability or dependent services. A practical mitigation pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes a configuration, a deterministic verifier checks policy/safety, and an automated repair step attempts to fix violations before apply. Despite increasing adoption, there is little preregistered, artifact‑archived evidence quantifying the verifier/repair marginal effect under deterministic, reproducible selection and analysis rules. We designed a confirmatory paired experiment to isolate that marginal effect. Research question: To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and what are the attendant cost/latency tradeoffs under a fixed generator output? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired evaluation (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) with deterministic selection and complete artifact hashing; (2) a reproducible ceiling/null empirical outcome (both arms 200/200 validator‑compliant) together with archives for bit‑exact replay; (3) concrete, artifact‑grounded recommendations for sampling and estimand choices that reveal verifier value in future studies.
sections.related_work: Generate–validate–repair architectures and verifier‑guided agentic NetOps have been proposed and evaluated in several recent works that emphasize integrating formal verification or deterministic validators to bound LLM risk (e.g., the Cornetto line of work and recent tool‑augmented agent systems). Prior benchmarks frequently measure end‑to‑end success or model rankings, whereas operational value demands causal comparisons of verifier/repair machinery. Our study complements prior architectures by providing a preregistered paired estimator with archived, machine‑verifiable artifacts enabling independent replay and alternative estimand computation.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental contract. The full preregistration is archived (preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) and fixes all design choices before observing results. Key design elements (frozen): paired design; K=200 tasks deterministically selected from an assembled public intent pool by computing SHA‑256(intent_string) and choosing the first 200 entries after filtering to intents the preregistered deterministic validator reports as covered; a single shared_initial_generation per task (both arms used the identical generator candidate) so the paired contrast isolates verifier+repair marginality; per‑task initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; requested_model = gpt-5-mini; maximum_model_calls = 400 (predeclared). The execution adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (see execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Task construction and inclusion. To ensure the verifier could meaningfully score candidates, the preregistration required inclusion only of intents for which the validator reported coverage; this inclusion rule is explicitly part of the preregistered sampling plan and therefore biases the sample toward validator‑covered intents (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). Execution logging and artifact capture. Every prompt, response, provider call trace, verifier trace, and per‑episode scoring JSON was captured and hashed; core fingerprints include execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = 79c91155...), and the full execution manifest with per‑file hashes (see artifact table). Analysis plan. The primary confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The prespecified test is an exact McNemar two‑sided test; uncertainty reported via paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) percentile CI. The analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and seeds are archived; analytic outputs and contingency table are in analysis/*.csv (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...).
sections.results: Execution summary. The run completed as preregistered: planned episodes 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks); completed episodes 400; failed episodes 0; model calls used = 200 (one shared generator call per task); repair pathway was not exercised (repair_applied=false across scoring JSONs). Primary outcome. The paired contingency table is n11=200 (both arms success), n10=0 (guarded only), n01=0 (baseline only), n00=0 (both fail). Observed marginal rates: baseline = 200/200 (100% validator‑compliant applies); guarded = 200/200 (100%). Inferential result: paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. Artifact pointers: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c...), and the per‑task scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/*.json (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...). Representative diagnostics. Each scoring JSON includes validator diagnostics used for auditing: parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, and a final_state snapshot that records the validator’s simulated post‑apply result (see execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json and execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json). Repair usage and costs. Because the validator accepted every shared_initial_candidate, the automated repair step was never invoked and the model_call budget consumed equals the number of tasks (200). Reproducibility metadata. Key artifact SHA‑256 fingerprints for deterministic replay: execution/raw_results.jsonl = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6; execution/model_configuration.json = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa; execution/task_manifest.jsonl = f1d447b7621f83208298f5c8d965bcdbba115e741f95a1efb92944347b35bbf0; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c.
sections.discussion: Interpreting a ceiling/null outcome. Under the preregistered contract the G→V→R marginal effect was zero: the verifier accepted every generator candidate and repairs were not used. This is a reproducible ceiling/null result for the specific sampling/model/validator regime—it does not imply verifiers are universally unnecessary. Three methodological variables explain why the sample produced no verifier‑exercising failures: (1) the inclusion rule explicitly filtered tasks to intents the deterministic validator reported as covered; that policy reduces the prevalence of validator failures and therefore reduces the opportunity for repair to alter outcomes, (2) the shared_initial_generation design intentionally fixes generator output across arms to isolate verifier+repair marginality; an end‑to‑end closed‑loop estimand where the generator may regenerate after a validator failure would measure a different, operationally relevant quantity, and (3) the single requested model (gpt-5-mini) and the deterministic validator implementation together determine the observed ceiling. Practical consequences for future studies. To assess operational verifier value one should (i) sample failure‑rich or adversarial intents (explicitly include validator‑uncovered tasks or historical incident corpora), (ii) consider closed‑loop estimands that let the generator iterate after validator failures, and (iii) evaluate across multiple generator strengths and alternative validator implementations. Per‑task difficulty and verifier coverage. Each scoring JSON contains a per‑task difficulty label (difficulty.level) and validator diagnostics (validation_before/after). The run’s artifacts therefore permit deterministic aggregation of difficulty and coverage counts. We did not compute the full K=200 aggregated difficulty summary during the main analysis pass; the per‑task fields are present in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256s above) and can be aggregated deterministically by parsing those files. For transparency we report the difficulty labels and diagnostic counts for the representative tasks archived in the manuscript bundle: task-000001 (difficulty.level = "medium"), task-000002 ("hard"), task-000003 ("hard"), task-000004 ("very_hard"), task-000005 ("hard"), task-000006 ("very_hard"). Those representative entries are preserved to illustrate the validator metadata schema; full K=200 aggregation is reproducible from the archived artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json). Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial_generation design isolates verifier marginality but precludes generator adaptation. Construct validity: our binary validator outcome depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would underrepresent regressions. External validity: single model, synthetic deterministic selection filtered to validator coverage, and no adversarial sampling limit generalization to production distributions. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency (all successes) yields trivial point estimate and CI; this correctly reflects the sampled regime and its low variance.
sections.conclusion: In this fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered pool; shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), both baseline and guarded arms achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes compared with accepting the LLM suggestion directly) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...; provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). We therefore recommend that future confirmatory work (i) deliberately sample failure‑rich or adversarial intents, (ii) consider closed‑loop generator–validator estimands that allow regeneration on validator failure, and (iii) report aggregated per‑task difficulty and validator coverage statistics (those fields are available in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl for deterministic aggregation). All artifacts required to reproduce, reaggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed to facilitate independent audit and exploration of verifier utility under alternative contracts.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for true operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
